page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz, provisioned as 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via dedicated hyperthreading on a KVM hypervisor. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes show moderate single-thread capabilities juxtaposed with constrained multi-core throughput due to the low core count. The instance achieved an average-tier Geekbench single-core score of 1,495.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 2,680.19, and solid single-threaded gzip compression at 25.49 GB/sec. Instruction set support includes AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, resulting in an average PassMark CPU encryption score of 4,292.03. However, heavier parallel and memory-intensive loads place in lower percentiles, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 3,370.0, a PassMark CPU score of 6,143.61, and uncached large-block write bandwidth of 15.45 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the absence of local storage and modest parallel bandwidth, making the system ill-suited for large-scale data engines, high-demand LLM token generation, or massive database transactions. Instead, its dedicated compute design provides predictable entry-level processing capability suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, small CI/CD tasks, and basic background compute tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance includes no local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the server delivers mid-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,495.0 and reliable cryptographic throughput via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets. However, multi-core and memory-heavy workloads fall into lower performance tiers due to the 4-vCPU resource envelope, as reflected by a 3,370.0 Geekbench multi-core score and 15.45 GB/sec large-block uncached write speed. With its 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio, ecs.c7a.xlarge is best suited for entry-level computational tasks, standard web serving, small CI/CD builds, and microservices.
